extracted.intended_audience: law students and legal practitioners (including patent attorneys and librarians)
extracted.subtask_description: A publisher's catalogue / bookseller's listing of legal reference works across many areas (including patents, designs, trade marks). Useful for selecting up-to-date treatises, statutes, digests, and practice manuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Acts, Rules and Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal treatises (esp. on statutory subjects like patents, designs, trade marks) should include the relevant Act text, the accompanying Rules, and practical Forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example phrasing from the page: 'Patents, Designs and Trade Marks Acts 1883, with Notes and Index to the Act, Rules and Forms.' Several listings advertise the Act plus Rules and Forms as part of the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes and explanatory commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Books should contain introductions, critical and explanatory notes that clarify the statute or subject-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page examples: 'with an Introduction and Critical and Explanatory Notes' (Married Women's Property); reviews praise 'excellent critical and explanatory notes'. Notes are presented as essential for understanding and practical use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices of statutes and statutory material
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatises should include appendices collecting statutes, schedules, statutory enactments, and related statutory material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple entries advertize 'Appendix of Statutes', 'The Statutes in full', or appendices containing statutory enactments relevant to the topic (e.g., Libel and Slander entry: 'With Appendix of Statutes including the Newspaper Libel and Registration Act, 1881').

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection or digest of leading cases with notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference works should provide digests or selections of leading judicial decisions, often with brief notes or summaries of each case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Chambers' Digest ... With Notes of 1260 leading Cases' and many 'Leading Cases' titles; the presence of case digests is repeatedly emphasized as a feature of utility to students and practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical directions, forms and precedents for practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical manuals should supply procedural directions, forms, and precedents that practitioners can use in actual practice (e.g., registry procedures, pleading forms, precedents of injunctions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on the page: 'Including Practical Directions to Solicitors for Proceedings in the Registry', 'Precedents of Pleadings, with Notes and Rules', 'Appendices containing precedents of Injunctions.' These features are highlighted as making a book 'practical' and 'useful'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Up‑to‑date supplements and revised editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Good legal publications are kept current via new editions, revisions, and supplements correcting to the latest date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page notes: 'Second Edition', 'Fourth Edition — Thoroughly revised', 'Supplement corrected to February 8, 1883'; reviewers praise works that have been brought 'well up to date'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive indexes, tables and other finding aids
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of a copious index, tables (e.g., Table of Offences and Punishments), chronological or alphabetical arrangement, and other finding aids is an expected feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'A Copious Index', 'A Table of Offences and Punishments', 'arranged in Alphabetical and Chronological order, with Notes thereon' (Chitty's Collection). Indexes are repeatedly cited as important for reference use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible presentation and clear language
rubrics_metrics.description: Works intended for students and practitioners should be presented in a clear, concise, and accessible manner to aid comprehension and practical use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review quotations on the page: 'information is presented in a most accessible form', 'language is simple, concise, and clear', 'very simple and practical' — readability is considered a quality metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of related jurisdictions and foreign law where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: For topics with international aspects (e.g., trade marks, patent law comparative matters), good works include coverage of foreign, colonial, or international statutes and decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Trade Marks: Notes on the British, Foreign, and Colonial Laws relating thereto' and 'Thompson's Handbook of Patent Law of all Countries' — indicating scope across jurisdictions as a desirable feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of illustrative forms, practical rules and procedural notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Books of practice should include illustrative forms, practical rules, and procedural notes (e.g., Rules of the Supreme Court, forms in use in registries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries cite 'Rules and Forms', 'Forms of Orders in use in the Chancery Registrar's Office', 'Rules of the Supreme Court' — these procedural inclusions are marketed as essential for practitioner use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices of cases, precedents and cross‑referenced materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Helpful reference books append collections of precedents, forms, and cross‑references to related acts and cases to make the work a one‑stop resource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several titles promise appendices and digests: 'Appendices containing precedents of Injunctions', 'Digest of Cases ... decided in the Courts of the United Kingdom, India, the Colonies, and the United States' — emphasis on appended materials that broaden practical utility.
